hypothesis: The target rules explicitly end an earlier assist chain at a defensive pass. A successful type1 opposing-team pass is positive passing evidence; requiring a second earlier completed pass in the previous version was extra corroboration, not a target-rule condition. Test a separate predictor using one successful defensive pass as the boundary, retaining all subsequent attacking actors. No new awards, no missing-marker zeros.
guards: Normal goals only, no penalty/direct free kick/own goal. Last successful opposing pass strictly before the goal in the same period and within60seconds; its player must be identified. Include all events at the boundary timestamp. Reject missing actor/type/team information except the unchanged explicit administrative types, deleted events, coverage interruptions, other goals or fouls. Unique scoring-team participant identity required. Do not infer physical contact counts from duel markers.
validation: Freeze before comparing the same full2025 scoring-team population. At least20 applicable unresolved control goals and20 one-goal controls, zero incompatible team vectors, zero one-goal errors, zero contradictions of protected awards or positive source candidate bounds. Same minimum and error gates as the previous version. Previously seen/shared-Opta outcomes are regression, not an untouched holdout or independent provider validation.
application: If qualified, apply only to unresolved pre2025 goals with complete scorer/team coverage. Retain all previous exclusions and known totals. Explicit source conflicts block the rule, not just the conflicting examples. RawFPL, approved corrections, frozen controls and locked scoring remain unchanged.
